body.text:
大家好！我是美国人，在上海学中文已经一年了。上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，我们在西湖旁边走路了三个小时，风景非常好看。

但是我有一个问题：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得它太酸了，我不是很喜欢吃。是不是我点得不对？还有什么杭州菜你们推荐我试一试吗？谢谢！
body.background: A post on Xiaohongshu after my weekend in Hangzhou.

out.title: 回复在杭州问西湖醋鱼的美国朋友
out.audience: Chinese travel-lovers and locals who follow food and travel notes
out.purpose: Share a Hangzhou weekend and ask which dishes to try

parts.problem: A Chinese travel writer would show the scenery through its effect on the visitor, for example that it made them unwilling to leave. 风景非常好看 is a complete judgment with nothing behind it, so the praise is thin and the reader has nothing to picture.

readings.meaning: Everything this passage says now: every point, question, hedge and feeling in it stays; only how it is put changes.

parts.problem: Here 有一个问题 announces a real difficulty, and Chinese readers expect the writer to say what went wrong, such as bad service, a bad dish or a bad experience. The post then asks only whether the writer ordered the wrong thing, so the frame promises more than the question delivers.
parts.question: Was this a real problem with the meal, or just a question about your taste?

readings.label: small taste question
readings.meaning: Only a question about my own taste and order.

parts.problem: 太…了 is a flat verdict, and with 西湖醋鱼, a famous Hangzhou dish, a local reader may hear the dish itself judged as wrong, not just unsuited to the writer. Stated this way, the criticism is much harsher than the writer seems to intend.

out.reader: 就一句好看？那西湖到底让你们什么感觉？
out.ref: 上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，在西湖[边][一走就是]三个小时，风景[美得让]人[舍不得]停下来。
alts: 上个周末和朋友去杭州逛了一天，在西湖边走了整整三个小时，景色美到不想走。
上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，在西湖边走着走着就是三个小时，景色好到让人不想走。
out.construct: 景色美得让人 + 动词 (so beautiful it made me ___)

why.label: 一走
why.note: 一走就是 makes the long walk the story: you lost track of time. Plain 走了三个小时 only reports how long it took, which is the flat fact the writer already has.

why.label: 美得
why.note: 美得让人 turns the beauty into its effect on people. 风景非常好看 is a verdict the reader has to take on trust, while 美得 lets them feel it.

why.label: 舍不得
why.note: Saying you didn't want to stop shows the scenery through your reaction, the way travel posts usually do. Here 舍不得 means you were reluctant to leave, not that you were sad.

why.label: 在西湖边
why.note: 边 is how people here say where a walk happened (西湖边). 西湖旁边 is understood, but it sounds like a map description, not a stroll.

out.prompt: Show the West Lake walk and how lovely the scenery was, through what it did to you.
out.success: 哈哈，这下我也想去西湖走走了！

out.construct: 我有个问题想请教X（I have a question I'd like to ask X）

why.label: 有个
why.note: Locals say 有个 in casual posts, where 有一个 reads a little stiff and formal. The writer's casual voice fits 有个 here.

why.label: 想请教大家
why.note: Where the draft says 有一个问题, which tells readers something has gone wrong, 想请教大家 says you want their advice. It keeps the question but drops the complaint frame, so the reader expects a request for help, not a grievance.

out.prompt: Rewrite the opening line so it fits the question you're asking.
out.success: 哈哈原来是问点菜的事，我来帮你！

out.plan: Open by stating that you have one small matter, then follow with a clause saying what you want from readers, so the frame signals a polite request rather than a complaint. Put the verb for asking for advice just before the word for the audience, so the sentence ends by addressing everyone and the tone stays light.

out.gloss: A verb meaning to ask someone more knowledgeable for advice or explanation. It takes a person as its object and is polite, somewhat humble, and used for seeking guidance rather than casual questions.
out.example: 我想请教一下王老师，这道题应该怎么做。

out.gloss: A casual, informal verb meaning to ask someone about something to find out information. It is the reduplicated form of 问 and sounds lighter and less formal than 请教, with no sense of deference.
out.example: 你去问问妈妈，晚饭想吃什么。

out.gloss: A noun meaning a question or doubt that one is unsure about and wants answered. It is used with verbs like 有 (have), 提出 (raise), or 解答 (answer), and is narrower than the general word 问题.
out.example: 看完说明书，他心里还有些疑问，就打电话去客服问清楚。

out.gloss: A pronoun meaning everyone or all of the people in a group, including the speaker or addressed group as a whole. It is neutral in register and is often used to address a group of people collectively.
out.example: 今天下雨，大家都带着伞去上班了。

out.reader: 咦？西湖醋鱼不是很有名吗？怎么会酸？
out.ref: 但是我有个问题想请教大家：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得我吃到的[这盘]酸[得不对劲]，[应该]是没做好吧，我不是很喜欢吃。
alts: 可是我觉得我吃到的这盘酸得不对味，好像是做得不到位，我不是很喜欢吃。
可是我觉得我吃到的这盘味道不太对，应该是厨房没做好，我不是很喜欢吃。
out.construct: 我吃到的这盘+ adjective (the one I got was + adjective)

why.label: 这盘
why.note: Points at the plate the writer was served, so the problem is this one batch, not the dish itself. 太酸了 with 它 pins the flaw on 西湖醋鱼 as a dish, which is the harsh reading the writer did not intend.

why.label: 不对劲
why.note: Means 'off' or 'not right', which says the plate came out wrong. 太酸了 is a flat verdict on taste. Compare: 酸得不对劲 suggests something went wrong in the making, while 太酸了 suggests the dish is simply too sour.

why.label: 应该
why.note: Softens the cause into a guess, which fits a foreigner's guess about a local dish. Without it, 没做好 becomes a firm accusation against the kitchen; with it, the writer is still asking, as the 请教 frame sets up.

out.prompt: Rewrite your sentence about the dish you ordered, keeping your friendly voice.
out.success: 原来是没做好啊，那我下次去试试！

out.reader: 啊？西湖醋鱼是这个味道吗？那你们是怎么做的？
out.tutor: Your 太酸了。 is a flat verdict, so readers will take it as you calling 西湖醋鱼 itself too sour, not that the plate you were served came out wrong. The waiter's praise also has no contrast set against it, so the "but" you meant is gone.
out.repaired: 可是我觉得我吃到的这盘酸得不对劲，应该是没做好吧。是不是我点得不对？

out.tutor: That's the same as your last try. Your 太酸了。 is a flat verdict, so readers will take it as you calling 西湖醋鱼 itself too sour, not that the plate you were served came out wrong. The waiter's praise also has no contrast set against it, so the "but" you meant is gone.
out.repaired: 可是我觉得我吃到的这盘酸得不对劲，应该是没做好吧。是不是我点得不对？

out.plan: Keep your contrast with the waiter's praise, but put the "but" before your opinion so the two stand side by side. Then describe the plate you were served as going wrong, and give that as the reason you didn't enjoy it, so the fault lies with that plate and not with the dish itself. Finish with your own preference, stated lightly.
out.example: 同学说这家书店的咖啡很好喝，[可是我觉得]我买的这杯[不对劲]，[应该是][没做好]吧。

body.q: Why can't I keep what I wrote?

out.answer: Bare 太酸了 sounds like you're saying 西湖醋鱼 is too sour, period, and locals will hear that as a dig at the dish itself. You can keep the idea of too sour if you tie it to this plate, like 我吃到的这盘好像太酸了. The reference wording also keeps the contrast with the waiter's praise, which is what makes your 可是 work, so I'd stick with it.

body.final: 但是我有个问题想请教大家：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得我吃到的这盘酸得不对劲，应该是没做好吧，我不是很喜欢吃。

out.reader: 你是说点错菜了，还是这家店不好呀？
out.ref: 我是不是[应该]点[别的]菜[才对]？
alts: 我是不是该点别的菜呀？
我是不是应该换一个菜点？
out.construct: 我是不是应该 + verb + 才对？ (should I have … instead?)

why.label: 应该
why.note: States what the writer thinks should have happened. Their draft only says the order was wrong (点得不对), which leaves the readers guessing what the right order would have been. 应该 names the expectation, so readers can answer with a suggestion.

why.label: 别的
why.note: Everyday spoken word for 'other, something else'. A learner might write 其他的 or 另一个, which sound more written or more like a menu-counter. 别的 fits a casual travel note.

why.label: 才对
why.note: Closes the question with the sense of 'the right thing would have been…'. It replaces the vague 不对 with a clear alternative, and it sounds natural at the end of a 是不是 question. Example: 你早点说才对.

out.prompt: Rewrite this question so readers can tell what you wish you had ordered instead.
out.success: 哈哈，醋鱼确实挺酸的，下次点别的吧～

out.construct: 是不是这道菜本来就该 + adjective？

why.label: 本来
why.note: 本来 means 'originally / by nature', so it asks what the dish is like in itself. A learner would likely write 我点得不对 or 点错了, which changes the question to whether the order was wrong. 本来 keeps it on the taste.

why.label: 该
why.note: 该 means 'is supposed to', which gives the standard for the dish. A learner might write 应该, but 应该 is a guess ('should probably'), and the writer is asking what the dish is meant to be like, not guessing.

out.prompt: Write the one question you really want answered: is this sourness the way the dish is meant to be?

out.construct: 等我下次去X的时候 (When I visit X next time)

why.label: 等我下次去杭州的时候
why.note: The post as it stands reads like a question about now. 等我下次去… sets the future trip, and 的时候 frames it as the time you will be there. Without it, readers can't tell whether you're asking for a plan or just curious.

why.label: 杭州菜
why.note: Keep the writer's 杭州菜 here. Learners often switch to 杭州的菜 or 名菜; the writer's wording is simpler and reads naturally in this post.

out.construct: 下次再去X，还有哪些X值得点？ (next time I go to X, which X are worth ordering?)

why.label: 下次
why.note: Putting 下次 first makes the trip explicitly future. Without it, the sentence reads as a general question about Hangzhou food, which is what the reader was puzzled by.

why.label: 值得点
why.note: Means 'worth ordering', which is what the writer wants to know. 'Try' (试一试) only means sampling; 值得点 tells readers she wants the ones to order on a visit.

why.label: 推荐一下呗
why.note: Casual and polite for asking a community for recommendations. 你们推荐我试一试 is a literal translation and sounds stiff; 你们推荐一下呗 keeps the request light.

out.prompt: Ask the readers which other Hangzhou dishes to order on your next visit.

out.tutor: Your frame "但是我有一个问题：" tells readers that something went wrong, so they expect a complaint about the dish or service. But the post only asks whether you ordered the wrong dish and what else to try, and it never says the question is for readers to answer.

out.closing: 你好！欢迎来杭州，还能在西湖边走三个小时，说明你是真的爱上这座城了。西湖醋鱼本来就是酸甜口的，醋和糖的比例讲究"醋香而不冲"，但你吃到的如果酸得发冲，那店里可能确实没调好。下次可以试试龙井虾仁、东坡肉、叫花鸡，或者在老字号楼外楼点一份，口味都比较温和，应该会更合你的胃口。
